title: Opal Logistics - run-rate sensitivity and savings scenarios
summary: Customer-specific before/after cost analysis for Opal Logistics showing three run-rate sensitivity scenarios (conservative/likely/aggressive) and recommended Redwood Optimize levers (batching, prefix caching, int8 quantization, model variant routing). Estimated median savings: ~56% run-rate reduction; time-to-implement: 3-6 weeks.
content:
Background:
Opal Logistics is running a multi-feature LLM pipeline (chat assistant for logistics ops + embeddings for search + short-form summarization) with steady growth in Q4–Q1. This doc translates the raw telemetry we received (token distribution, QPS patterns, average session lengths) into a set of before/after cost projections and a short implementation playbook for Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Goals for this analysis:
- Produce a defensible monthly cost comparison (baseline vs optimized) at current run-rate and two growth scenarios.
- Show sensitivity to three operational levers: batching, prefix (KV) caching, and quantization/model variant switch.
- Provide prioritized implementation steps with expected timeline and risk notes.

Key telemetry inputs (from Opal telemetry export, week of 2025-02-02):
- Average sustained QPS (user-facing generation requests): 18 req/s (peak 65 req/s for 10% of day)
- Average tokens/request (generation side): 420 tokens total (prompt 80 tokens, generation 340 tokens)
- Embedding calls: 120k per month (short, 512-dim)
- Average session length (chat): 3 turns (2 user, 1 system assistant-generated continuation)
- Current model: 70B dense variant deployed self-hosted (Opal Dedicated) with no prefix caching, minimal batching (per-request dispatch), and FP16 serving
- Measured latency requirement: p95 < 700 ms for interactive routes

Assumptions used across calculations (called out here to make the spreadsheet auditable):
- Token pricing proxies: baseline runtime unit costs derived from Opal's committed GPU pool: $0.12 per 1k forward tokens (generation-side), $0.03 per 1k prompt tokens (smaller cost since shorter attention path), embeddings $0.0007 per vector (their current billing). These are internalized run-rate costs (inclusive of infra + license overhead) provided by Opal SRE team.
- Batching efficiency: moving from per-request dispatch to 32-token-aware micro-batching yields 28–42% per-token cost reduction on generation work depending on sequence length distribution. We use a conservative 30% reduction for the likely case.
- Prefix/KV caching: we assume 22% of tokens are repeated prefixes across sessions (templates, repeated manifest headers). Effective cache hit reduces avg generation tokens by 18% in practice (not full 22) because of partial overlap.
- Quantization/model switch: switching from FP16 70B -> int8 70B-compatible path (Redwood verified) yields ~40% lower per-token cost for generation kernels; an alternative we model is moving to a 33B int8 variant for non-critical routes (80% of traffic eligible), which yields ~60% per-token reduction for that slice but slight quality delta.
- Implementation overhead: engineering + testing effort estimated 3–6 weeks. No SLA change required for Dedicated.

Baseline monthly cost (current run-rate):
- Generation workload cost: calculation uses QPS*avg tokens*seconds/month conversion. For simplicity the spreadsheet uses measured monthly tokens = 320M generation tokens. Using the $0.12/1k baseline -> generation cost = $38,400/month.
- Prompt handling and control tokens: 63M tokens -> $1,890/month.
- Embeddings: 120k vectors -> $84/month.
- Misc overhead (replicas, GPU idling, storage, network egress approximation) applied as a 25% uplift -> $10,583.
- Total baseline monthly = $51,0? Actually compute: 38,400 + 1,890 + 84 = 40,374; + 25% uplift 10,094 -> total baseline approx $50,468/month. (Spreadsheet has line-level math for audit.)

Optimized recommendations (bundle):
1) Turn on Redwood prefix/KV caching for templated requests and session reuse (expected avg token reduction 18%). Prioritize chat template routes and manifest-heavy summary calls.
2) Enable dynamic micro-batching with a 12–32 token-aware window on hosted serving runtime; target mean batch size 18 for interactive routes.
3) Deploy int8 kernel profiles for the 70B family (benchmarked on Opal infra) for latency-sensitive routes; for low-criticality embedding-generation and bulk summarization routes, route to 33B-int8 variant where quality testing passes.
4) Route fallback policy: when latency SLO at p95 threatens, auto-fallthrough to a smaller variant (33B) for best-effort throughput.
5) Instrument objective metric (quality score via sampled prompts + fuzzed evaluation) to monitor delta from model switches.

Before / After headline numbers (monthly):
- Baseline: $50,468/month (as above)
- After Redwood Optimize (Likely case): Estimated token-level reductions combined: 30% batching effect *applied to generation kernels* + 18% caching reduction (applied to generation tokens before batching effects) + 40% int8 kernel improvement on remaining heavy-generation slice. Conservative composition: total run-rate reduction = 56% -> Estimated optimized monthly = $22,220/month.
- Conservative scenario (partial adoption + lower cache hits): 32% total reduction -> $34,300/month.
- Aggressive scenario (full routing, 80% of traffic to 33B int8 where quality acceptable, strong cache hit): 68% reduction -> $16,150/month.

Sensitivity matrix (select rows from spreadsheet):
- Variable: sustained QPS +/- 50% (9 req/s, 27 req/s) with likely-case optimizations yields: 9 req/s -> $13.3k/month; 27 req/s -> $33.3k/month (these scale roughly linear with tokens, with some nonlinearity from batching efficiency improving at higher QPS).
- Variable: cache hit rate +/- 10 percentage points (from 22% baseline): each +1% cache hit reduces monthly by ~0.9% after bundling.
- Variable: batch size mean (from 12 -> 32): per-token cost delta +/- up to 12% depending on seq length distribution.

Implementation plan (prioritized):
Week 0–1: instrument telemetry hooks (sampled prompts, token counts per route, session templates) + small A/B traffic slice (5%) to verify no quality regressions.
Week 2–3: enable prefix caching on chat routes (non-destructive). Run 2-week validation window and measure effective cache hit and real-world token reduction.
Week 3–5: roll out micro-batching in the serving runtime for interactive routes, with latency-safe windowing and early flush. Tune parameters to preserve p95 SLO.
Week 4–6: enable int8 kernels for 70B for latency-sensitive routes; simultaneously run quality evaluation suite. If 33B variant is acceptable, deploy routing rule for non-SLO critical routes.
Week 6–8: widen rollout to 50–100% based on results, enable cost dashboards and daily alerts for token spend deltas.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regression from model variant switch: mitigate with shadow traffic and offline evals; keep human-in-loop gating for first 2 weeks.
- Latency SLO breaches after batching: mitigate with early-flush heuristics and p95 guardrails (fallback to single-request path when latency > threshold).
- Infrastructure constraints: verify headroom on Dedicated GPU pool to ensure micro-batching doesn't spike memory pressure; Redwood runtime profiling required pre-rollout.

Customer-facing summary (one-paragraph):
If Opal implements the recommended Redwood Optimize bundle (prefix caching, batching, int8 kernels, and selective model routing) we estimate a median monthly run-rate reduction of ~56%, moving current spend from ~$50k/month to ~$22k/month at current volume. Conservative planning should assume a 32% uplift reduction initially; the full savings pathway requires 6–8 weeks of incremental rollout and validation.

Next steps / immediate asks for Opal team:
- Confirm access to the telemetry exports (token-level traces and route tags) so we can populate the shared spreadsheet (SavingsModel_v3).
- JW (Opal infra lead) to greenlight a 5% shadow/AB slice for the first caching experiment.
- Schedule a 30-minute sync for engineering pairing next week (Priya + Jonah + Opal infra) to review gating metrics and rollout playbook.

Appendix A — quick math snapshot (spreadsheet rows):
- Monthly generation tokens (measured) = 320,000,000
- Baseline per-1k token cost = $0.12 -> $38,400
- After-cache effective tokens = 320M * (1 - 0.18) = 262.4M
- After-batching & int8 effective cost (composite) ~ 56% reduction -> final cost computed as above.

Appendix B — validation tests we will run during rollout:
- Quality: 2k sampled prompts + human pass/fail, automatic metric (ROUGE/EMB similarity) thresholds
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 across routing rules; auto-fallback on p95 > 700ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows
- Cost monitoring: daily rolling 7-day spend forecast + alert on >20% deviation from expected run-rate after changes

Notes on spreadsheet: the linked XLSX contains 5 tabs: telemetry, baseline-calc, optimize-model, scenarios, rollout-runbook. The doc above mirrors the likely-case tab and sensitivity slices. Please refer to the S3 link in linked_artifacts for line-by-line formulas.

Author: Priya Desai (op-ads, product-optimize). This is a working draft for Opal leadership and expected to be iterated after the first telemetry re-run post caching experiment.

Unresolved questions for Opal infra team:
- Confirm the percent of templated traffic (we used 22% as an assumed value; measurement may change the savings materially).
- Any contractual limits on model variant usage across their Dedicated pool? If licensing forbids multiple concurrent variants, the routing plan needs rework.

End of doc.
